cards.question: A gift card that covers part of an order leaves the rest unpaid

blocks.paragraph: How a split payment should look to a customer is a shop-experience call, and only you can decide how much surprise at checkout is acceptable.
A gift card that covers only part of an order is spent, and checkout then asks for a second payment without having said so first.
A customer with a small gift card may reach the end of checkout and be asked for a second payment they did not expect.

options.label: Keep it
options.consequence: Customers with a small gift card may reach the end of checkout and be asked for a payment they did not expect; some will leave.

options.label: Fix in a follow-up
options.consequence: The stack ships with the surprise second payment for now; a follow-up adds a notice before it, with a revisit date.

options.label: Fix before merge
options.consequence: The stack goes back to show the remaining amount before the customer pays, and returns with a new sheet.

recommendation.reason: A surprise second payment loses the sale.
